headline: India's Sensex Gains 20% in Dollar Terms Driven by Record FPI Inflows
summary: India's Sensex index has surged 20% in dollar terms this quarter, supported by record foreign portfolio investor buying exceeding ₹1.18 lakh crore in November across 13 consecutive trading sessions.
why: The BSE Sensex is a primary benchmark index for Indian equities, reflecting foreign institutional capital flows into emerging markets.

impacts.name: BSE SENSEX
impacts.why: Record foreign institutional investment purchases pushed the benchmark equity index significantly higher.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Strong foreign portfolio investor inflows of over ₹1.18 lakh crore fueled a 20% dollar-denominated quarterly surge in the Sensex.
